models.architecture_or_algorithm: ensemble random projection (RP) model with proportionalized split amino acid composition (PSAAC) and conventional sequence-based features
models.input_features: PSAAC features capturing residue patterns at N- and C-termini and sequence order from middle fragments, plus conventional sequence-based features
models.candidate_reason: Novel AMP prediction model with publicly available code, outperforms existing methods in benchmark; suitable for inclusion.
models.evidence: From PMID 39573886 abstract: 'SAMP, an ensemble random projection (RP) based computational model that leverages a new type of feature called proportionalized split amino acid composition (PSAAC)... Python package freely available at https://github.com/wan-mlab/SAMP.' Also corroborated by preprint PMID 38712184.

important_evidence: SAMP: ensemble random projection model with PSAAC features, publicly available at https://github.com/wan-mlab/SAMP, outperforms iAMPpred and AMPScanner V2 in accuracy, MCC, G-measure, F1-score.
AmpGram: Random Forest with n-grams, first tool for longer AMPs and proteomic screening, available as web-server and R package, outperforms AMPScanner, CAMPR3R, iAMPpred.
Review (FEBS Open Bio 2025) lists multiple AMP prediction tools: AMPScanner V2, ampir, Macrel, Ensemble-AMPPred, DBAASP, CancerGram, PPTPP, MLBP, Deep2Pep.
AmpGram benchmarked on APD3 and DAMPD datasets; SAMP benchmarked on balanced and imbalanced datasets.
